newsitem.title: UK: Diana's call for mine ban upsets British ministers.
newsitem.headline: Diana's call for mine ban upsets British ministers.

text.p: Princess Diana's call for a worldwide ban on anti-personnel landmines during a visit to Angola upset some British ministers who feared it could interfere with government policy.

Dubbed the "princess of peace" on Tuesday after she met crippled casualties of Angola's 20-year war, she condemned the "horrific injuries" and urged countries to adopt an international ban on the "hideous weapons".
But ministers back in Britain described her comments as "ill-advised" and "not helpful".

"She was ill-advised and is not being helpful or realistic. Britain is one of the goodies on landmines and we are helping to draw up a sensible worldwide compromise package. We do not need a loose cannon like her," an unnamed minister told The Times newspaper.

Diana's visit on behalf of the Red Cross to highlight the problem of the landmines in Angola, which still has nine million mines and the world's highest rate of amputees, had been sanctioned by the government.
The princess had also been fully briefed on government policy before she left.
The Daily Telegraph said ministers were upset that Diana had used the visit to adopt a "partisan" stand which could be interpreted as being biased towards the Labour Party.
The ruling Conservatives, who must call an election by May, are trailing the opposition Labour Party by up to 20 points according to the latest opinion polls.
The Red Cross wants Britain to declare a national ban and to destroy its exisiting stock of landmines but the government has said a ban should be imposed internationally.
"The ministry of defence believes that the Red Cross position, backed by the princess is "unrealistic'," according to the Daily Telegraph.
Labour's defence spokesman Tom Clark welcomed Diana's comments and said he was amazed Diana was prepared to speak up against the government.
"What the princess is trying to do is raise awareness and we wish her well. We are pleased that she has taken the same view as us," he told journalists.
Diana's Angola visit on behalf of the Red Cross marks a major departure from the usual gala events she has attended on behalf of her charities since her divorce from Prince Charles last August.
Instead of wearing designer gowns and dining with the rich and famous Diana donned casual attire to meet people from some of the poorest areas in Angola.

Visibly moved by many of the people she met, Diana is finally fulfilling her expressed desire to be Britain's "Queen of Hearts," an ambition she confessed to in a television interview in November 1995.
